claims.title: New iPad Pro by the end of April
claims.sourceState: Public quotation of the March 10 newsletter
claims.summary: A public quotation placed the new iPad hardware around the end of March or in April. The iPad Pro arrived in May.
claims.context: This records the earlier expectation separately from F-002’s revised May window. It isolates the iPad Pro arrival claim; other specifications and accessories in the report are not graded here.
claims.quote: Look for that new hardware around the end of March or in April
claims.assessment: Using April 30 as the last day of the stated month, the May 7 announcement was 7 days late and May 15 customer availability was 15 days late. Both release-stage readings miss the month. The hardware did arrive; that does not turn the dated forecast into a success.
claims.review: Provisional assessment by the project assistant. April 30 is the explicit calendar-month reading used retrospectively; no grace period was added to “around.” This evaluates the published expectation, not whether Apple changed an internal plan.
claims.clarityNote: The release stage is ambiguous, but both announcement and availability fall after April. The timing-miss verdict is unchanged under those two readings.
claims.criteria: Interpret “or in April” as ending April 30, 2024, with no post-hoc grace period. Test announcement and customer availability separately because “new hardware” does not uniquely identify a release stage.

timing.label: Late
timing.note: 7 days late to announcement; 15 days late to customer availability. These are two milestone readings, not a statistical confidence interval.

checks.finding: The March 11 article quotes the March 10 newsletter’s end-of-March or April expectation.
